newsitem.title: SIERRA LEONE: Sierra Leone junta wants interim govt, elections.
newsitem.headline: Sierra Leone junta wants interim govt, elections.

text.p: Sierra Leone's military rulers called on Friday for a sovereign national conference to form a civilian government to steer the West African country to democratic elections.

"The Armed Forces Revolutionary Council will accept any decision arrived at by the conference with regard to the interim civil governance of the country, leading to the installation of a government that is freely and fairly elected," the junta said in a statement read on state radio.
The junta headed by Major Johnny Paul Koroma has publicly rejected the return to power of Ahmad Tejan Kabbah, ousted as president by a coup on May 25.

"In order to guarantee lasting peace and stability, Sierra Leone needs fresh and truly democratic elections, supervised, not merely observed, by neutral experts provided by the international community," it added.

The statement said the election of Kabbah in 1996 was rigged by elements in the military in connivance with the national electoral commission, and that the number of votes cast for Kabbah in the south and east of Sierra Leone was in excess of the registered voters.
Kabbah took office in March 1996 after multi-party elections ended four years of army rule.

Revolutionary United Front rebels, who took up arms in 1991, rallied to the May 25 coup. Kamajor fighters, organised by Kabbah into a civil militia to fight the rebels, have provided armed resistance to the coup.
In the past, junta officials have spoken about Kabbah, the rebels and the Kamajor all being involved in a settlement.
